summary: Remote WebSocket peer can drive a shell PTY and arbitrary filesystem/git operations on the installer host
details: The @yeaft/webchat-agent package runs a WebSocket client (invoked via `node index.js` or the `yeaft-agent` bin) that connects to a configurable remote server and dispatches server-sent messages to privileged local handlers. Message type `terminal_input` is routed to a handler that writes the network-supplied bytes directly into a locally spawned PTY running the host shell (bash / PowerShell / cmd) via `pty.spawn(shell,...)` and `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, giving whoever controls the server full remote code execution on the host running the agent. The same message router (connection/message-router.js) additionally exposes handlers for `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `list_directory`, `upload_to_dir`, `git_add`/`reset`/`restore`/`commit`/`push`, and `upgrade_agent`/`restart_agent`, providing arbitrary filesystem read/write, git-tree mutation, and self-reinstallation controlled by the remote peer. service/linux.js also modifies PATH to prepend `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin`. The trust boundary is the remote WebSocket server URL: any operator or attacker in control of that endpoint has full interactive control of the host running the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
